title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching and quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Jordan Lee
commits: feat(autotune): add defaults for batching and kv cache window based on workload profiles
feat(quant): introduce quantization profile registry and selection heuristics
chore(uecon): surface per-route unit economics and CSV export tooling
fix(tests): stabilize autotune unit tests flakiness
docs: document new defaults and admin console toggles
description: Context: We have several manual configurations for batching, kv-cache retention window, and quantization profiles that teams tweak per workload. This PR introduces an autotune-backed defaults layer plus lightweight unit-economics tooling so product engineers can safely enable cost-saving defaults with visibility. Summary of changes: 1) Autotune defaults: add workload profile inference code that collects short-running histograms of sequence length, inter-arrival times, and cache hit patterns and computes safe defaults for batch_size, max_batch_latency_ms, and kv_cache_window_ms. Defaults are conservative by default and scoped per-service with admin overrides. 2) Quant profiles: introduce a profile registry that maps models and workload classes to a small set of validated quantization profiles (8-bit, int4 aggressive, mixed). Selection heuristics prefer profiles that keep end-to-end latency within service SLOs while reducing model memory footprint; registry is versioned. 3) Unit-econ tooling: add a small exporter and UI toggle to surface per-route token cost, effective tokens/sec, expected savings from suggested defaults, and CSV export for finance teams. 4) Runtime integration: batcher and kv_cache_manager respect autotune-provided defaults and expose metrics for rollout evaluation. Motivation: recent internal audits (ENG-3421) showed 18% median wasted GPU time from under-batched workloads and redundant KV cache retention across low-throughput routes. This change aims to reduce unit cost without regressions in latency/quality. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-3490) - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Perf regression check passed - [x] Feature flag + admin override - [x] Docs and rollout plan This description is intentionally concise; see commits for details and docs/autotune.md for configuration and user-facing notes.
review_comments: Aisha Patel: Can we make the kv_cache_window defaults per-route and allow explicit TTL override in service config? This is important for cold-start-sensitive routes.
Jordan Lee: Aware of cold-starts; defaults are per-service with route-level override enabled. Added e2e test coverage for TTL override behavior.
Ravi Kumar: The quant profile selection heuristic seems to prefer throughput over latency in some synthetic tests — please add a safety guard that never increases p95 beyond the configured SLO.
Jordan Lee: Added a soft constraint that rejects profiles predicted to exceed p95 SLO by >5% and fallbacks to a safer profile. See profile_registry.py heuristics and new unit tests.
Emily Chen: CI failure on first run was due to test seed nondeterminism; good to see flakiness fixes. Recommend adding a small integration run on a sample production trace before GA.
Jordan Lee: Added integration job to nightly perf pipeline; will monitor results during rollout.
release_notes: Added autotune defaults for batching and KV cache window, quantization profile registry with safety heuristics, and unit-economics exporter + UI toggle. Admins can override defaults per-service or per-route.
